analysis: Trial executed successfully but achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.4912, below the supplied 0.505 baseline by 0.0138. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.565, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.375, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.495. Electronics had the lowest absolute performance; category-level baseline scores were not supplied, so regressions cannot be assigned to individual categories. This result does not support the proposed improvement from sampled-softmax training. The metrics alone cannot isolate whether normalization, sampling, regularization, or checkpoint selection caused the shortfall. Allocated GPU time was 396.28 seconds.
code_summary: Trains one independent SASRec-derived model per category using seed 42 and unchanged prepared training/validation splits. Each model has two causal pre-norm transformer blocks, 96 hidden dimensions, two attention heads, length-64 histories, and dropout 0.2. Scores use normalized sequence/item embeddings, a learned temperature, and jointly learned item biases. Training uses sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 256 shared uniform negatives, masks observed training items, samples up to 24 transitions per history, and occasionally truncates training prefixes. AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, gradient clipping, and validation-based early stopping select exactly one checkpoint per category. The generated predictor routes by dataset and loads that category’s single trained checkpoint; no ensemble or separately fitted scores are used.
